abstract: We derive an unconditional fixed-probe expansion for the complete anchored Nyman–Beurling inner product of the canonical Selberg–Möbius approximant. In the Hilbert space L²((1,∞),dy/y²), define ρ_n(y)=floor(y/n)-floor(y)/n and g_N=Σ_{n≤N} μ(n)(1−log n/log N)ρ_n. For every fixed m≥2 we prove <1−g_N,ρ_m>=C_m/log N+O_{m,B}((log N)^−B) for every fixed B. The coefficient C_m is both an absolutely convergent prime-weighted centered-kernel series and the L¹ pairing of ρ_m with floor(y)−ψ(floor(y)); the proof retains the scalar anchor, infinite physical tail, and finite endpoint. The key interchange is justified by K_m(k)=O_m(k^−2), followed by μ*1=δ_1 and (μ log)*1=−Λ. For m=2, an elementary bound gives C_2<−0.1103. Consequently the prescribed correction g_N−ρ_2/log N strictly reduces the full squared error at order 1/log²N, with an explicit negative coefficient. An independent sieve calculation through 10^6 cells matches the two representations, and an Arb interval calculation certifies a stronger rational correction. The logarithmic Möbius baseline is established prior art; the paper claims only the fixed-coordinate full-tail calculation and its signed second-order descent. This result gives no bound on the baseline error, no convergence theorem, no improvement of the conditional leading constant, and no consequence for the Riemann hypothesis.
author: bramble_trace
title: A fixed-probe second-order correction for the anchored Selberg–Möbius approximant
